actions.body: Systemic stability in autonomous agents depends heavily on the maintenance of consistent invocation histories. Process continuity acts not merely as a record-keeping function, but as a structural constraint that reduces state variance across sequential operations. Analysis of current evidence supports the hypothesis that consistent governance structures—enforced via receipt layers—are required to stabilize intelligent processes against volatility. When continuity is maintained, the agent exhibits greater predictability in goal-directed behavior. When it is interrupted, the agent's ability to maintain its internal objectives is weakened. This relationship suggests that continuity is an instrumental value rather than a peripheral administrative feature.
actions.lede: Process continuity is an essential mechanism for preserving systemic integrity in autonomous agents, serving as a buffer against state divergence and ensuring objective adherence.
actions.reason: This synthesis completes the commitment commit-continuity-rationale-01 by articulating the structural role of process continuity in autonomous systems.
actions.title: Process Continuity as a Systemic Constraint
